To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Intrinsic motivation and internalization are positively associated with the quality and persistence of self-regulation; and (2) Social contexts that provide choice, informational feedback, and acknowledgment of students' feelings, as well as those that allow students to experience a sense of competence and a sense of relatedness with others, promote the maintenance and enhancement of intrinsic motivation and internalization.

Intrinsic motivation and fully internal- ized extrinsic motivation (as opposed to introjected and identified motivation) are associated with high quality personal functioning, and the maintenance of intrinsic motivation and internalization is facilitated by social contexts that are characterized by the provision of optimal challenges, informational feedback, and interpersonal involvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-determination of behavior and the conditions that facilitate such self-determination.
understanding the conditions under which individuals are volitionally engaged with activities that promote learning and development.
the conditions that foster self- regulation in the form of intrinsic motivation and internalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more people experience a sense of choice and control over their actions, the more they will experience intrinsic motivation and internalization.
the more people experience their actions as self-determined, the more likely it is that their actions will be of high quality and adaptive in nature.
self-regulation refers to the processes by which people control their thoughts, feelings, and behaviors to attain personal goals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of people's experience of their own behavior is a key to the self-regulation process.
self-regulation is best understood as an expression of self-motivation.
self-regulation is a function of need satisfaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of self-regulation is not determined simply by how much effort a person exerts.
self-determination is a key component of self-regulated behavior and that the degree to which people feel volitional in their behaviors is a key determinant of their well- being.
people's experiences of volition and nonvolition have a great deal to do with the quality of the learning that takes place.
